None of the provided papers directly address “Flek physics constraint adversarial attacks” as a specific named method beyond Flek’s work on physics-inspired adversarial attacks in particle/astroparticle physics. Paper [1] (MiniFool) proposes physics-inspired adversarial attacks that minimize a cost combining a χ²-based test statistic based on experimental uncertainties and deviation from a target score, and it is applied in particle/astroparticle settings and also on MNIST and CMS data.

More generally, other constraint-focused adversarial approaches in the list include physics-/constraint-enforcing frameworks such as CAP (which enforces domain-specific feature constraints via an augmented Lagrangian) [3], WAAPO for weather models with channel sparsity/spatial localization/smoothness constraints [4], relational adversarial attacks under integrity constraints [2], and physics-informed adversarial training for neural operators [5]. These differ from [1] by targeting different data/model types and using different constraint mechanisms.
